method.pinning: taskset -c 6 (a 5.1 GHz Zen 5 core; odd CPUs are the slower Zen 5c cores)
method.nice: nice -n 5 for timing runs; builds under nice with -j4
method.end_to_end: 8 rounds; each round runs every version once in rotating order; user-mode cycles from perf stat, minus a run with 0 passes to remove setup (signal synthesis, the encode that makes the packets)
method.criterion: 4 full runs of benches/opus_bench.rs per version, interleaved in rotating order; value per run is criterion's point estimate; crate config (20 samples, 0.5 s)
method.kernel_microbench: 6 rounds, rotating order; each value is the best of 15 timing loops
method.aa_noise: see aa_noise; build-to-build code layout effects measured earlier at about +-1%
method.build: cargo release profile defaults (opt-level 3, no LTO, codegen-units 16), default features (std, heap); no RUSTFLAGS, no target-cpu; SIMD paths chosen at run time (this CPU has AVX2, FMA, AVX-512)

kernels.note: round 2: explicit even/odd [f32; 8] lanes; 15-50% faster than the intrinsics kernel
elementwise; within noise

round 3 redesign: pulses decoded straight into the band (no scratch, no zeroing), energy as an exact integer (no float reduction); 3-14% faster than round 2. A padded 2-D U table and a min()-clamped index were tried and were slower
round 3: exact integer energy below 2^24 (always, K <= 128); SIMD kernels kept only as the fallback past 2^24; within noise

round 3 redesign: eight lags per sweep with broadcast taps and the old per-lag tap order; 8-22% faster. Round 2 4-lag plain shapes were +16..+32%; the 4-lag kernel stays as intrinsics for the 4..7 leftover lags
round 3: fixed-size delay lines for orders 8..24; 3-10% faster than upstream (round 1 safe indexing had been +4%)
round 3: zipped iterators cut the gap from +7..10% to about +3%; filling the buffers by push instead of clearing them gave nothing
round 2; one call per pitch search; within noise
round 1; within noise end to end
round 1; integer wrapping sums are order-free; LPC filter 40-53% faster
already plain Rust compiled with target_feature(avx) upstream
round 2 lane arrays +14..20%; round 3 batched all bands with the lane combine moved out of the hot loop (256-bit FMA confirmed): still +17%

lane arrays with inline sum (LLVM narrows to 128-bit), out-of-line sum (+4..42%), black_box barrier (+3..24%), lane-explicit scaling (+4..20%), 8-wide rotate reduction (still narrowed); faster only at n=176. Calls are per band with sequential dependencies, so batching does not apply
round 2 plain: +5..+28% for n <= 160
used only for 4..7 leftover lags after the 8-lag plain sweep
plain simple and 8-blocked: +8.6..+9.2% on a shift-3 backward MDCT; worth at most ~0.4% of decode
same reduction shape as renormalise; not converted
fold (+24..44%, 128-bit vpmaddwd), madd-shaped lane pairs (+25..+220%, vpshufb), 32-blocks (+8..10%, -7% at 64), 64-blocks (+44..71%), 32+16-blocks (+8..20%)
scores use rsqrt/rcp approximations; no exact formulation picks the same pulses, so encoder output would change. The crate's exact scalar search is 3x slower at n16/k8; not pursued
no ARM hardware to A/B; loads/stores go through bounds-checked wrappers

kernels_note: "after" microbench numbers measure the shipped version. For kernels kept as intrinsics, the plain-Rust gap quoted in "note" comes from this round's pinned A/B (scratchpad/kb.sh, scratchpad/cb.sh) against the safety build.
